---
engine: markdown
title: Add Transaction History
description: Extend the payment model with earlier transactions from the same account.
---

The [first model](../getting-started.qmd) reads one payment. Now add earlier
transactions from the same account, keeping the same prediction target.

The business question becomes more specific: how does this payment fit the
account's recent behavior? Previous visits to the same merchant, changes in
amount, and gaps between transactions can provide context. An **event
history** preserves those observations so the model can learn their
relationships. Compare it with your existing aggregate features to find out
whether that detail improves dispute prediction.

## Add A Collection To Each Record

Your application supplies a `recent_transactions` list alongside the current
payment:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
recent_transactions:
  - days_ago: 7
    amount: 32.00
    merchant: Station Cafe
  - days_ago: 1
    amount: 56.20
    merchant: North Market
disputed: false
```

Include only transactions known before the current payment. Order them from
oldest to newest. A payment with no earlier transactions has an empty list.

Order describes which transaction came first; `days_ago` describes elapsed
time. Consecutive history entries might be minutes or weeks apart, so make
the time gap explicit when it matters to the task.

## Describe The Collection With A Branch

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    recent_transactions=rf.Branch(
        length=32,
        overflow="tail",
        days_ago=rf.Number,
        amount=rf.Number,
        merchant=rf.Category,
    ),
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

`Branch` describes a collection of records with the same fields. This branch
keeps at most 32 transactions; `overflow="tail"` retains the last 32 in the
supplied order. The model combines their information with the current
payment's amount and merchant to predict `disputed`.

```{typst}
//| label: fig-payment-history-tutorial
//| fig-alt: "A payment combines its amount and merchant with a repeated recent_transactions branch containing days_ago, amount, and merchant. Disputed remains the prediction target."
//| fig-cap: "The payment gains a history; its prediction target stays the same."
#tree(node("payment", kind: "root", children: (
  node("amount", type: "Number"),
  node("merchant", type: "Category"),
  node("recent_transactions", kind: "branch", repeated: true, width: 165pt, children: (
    node("days_ago", type: "Number"),
    node("amount", type: "Number"),
    node("merchant", type: "Category"),
  )),
  node("disputed", kind: "target", type: "Boolean"),
)))
```

## Use The Same Training Steps

Train this new model with the history present in each record. Your application
supplies Parquet files with the nested structure shown above:

```python
data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    model=model,
    train="payments/train.parquet",
    validate="payments/validation.parquet",
)
model.fit(data, batch_size=128, max_epochs=20)
```

Prediction files have the same structure and omit `disputed`:

```python
requests = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    model=model,
    predict="payments/requests.parquet",
)
predictions = model.predict(datamodule=requests, batch_size=256, devices=1)
```

If your source uses different names or shapes, continue with
[Binding Data](../core-concepts/binding-data.qmd). To prepare these histories
from transaction tables, see [Preprocessing](../guides/preprocessors.qmd).

[Learning From Event Histories](../guides/learning-from-event-data.qmd)
extends this pattern to recurring payments and other future outcomes.
